Hi Alice — thanks for the quick note and the specific questions. Short summary up front: for most customers with bursty profiles we recommend a blended approach (modest annual commit to reserve capacity + pay-as-you-go for spikes) because it gives predictable base pricing and a cap on baseline unit costs while keeping burst flexibility. See the two options below.

Option A — Hybrid (recommended)
- Modest annual commit (example: $100k) that covers baseline steady-state usage; priced at a discounted per-token rate.
- Usage buffer: usage above commit billed at standard API rates or a negotiated uplift rate (we can cap uplift at X% for predictability).
- Activation: AWS Marketplace Private Offer can be activated within 24–48 hours after PO and Seller acceptance (typical).

Option B — Pure usage (fast to activate)
- No annual commitment; pay only for what you use.
- Higher per-token unit price but no long-term commitment.
- Activation: usually immediate once payment instrument is accepted by AWS.

Signature / signatory guidance
- For Private Offers the buyer signs the PO on their side. On the seller side, Redwood signs the Private Offer acceptance (our authorized sales lead). For larger deals (> $250k) we typically have a sales leader + legal countersign on our internal side. From a practical standpoint, the Name on the AWS Private Offer acceptance will be Redwood Inference, Inc.

Next steps I recommend:
1) Decide which pricing band you prefer (Hybrid vs Pure usage) and an approximate annual commit number.
2) Share your internal signer names/emails so we can map approval lanes for activation.
3) If good, I’ll send a draft PO (PDF) and a DocuSign link for Redwood acceptance.

I’m attaching a short draft PO and an evidence checklist we usually provide to procurement. Happy to hop on a 20-min sync if needed.
